generatedProse.concept-context: In sport and exercise science, this runs through every lab report, case study and essay you write. When you cite a study on training load or a model of motor learning, three things happen together. You hold the values, you choose the reference with purpose, and you judge whether to quote a precise protocol or paraphrase a result. Your reference list then shows a reader both the range of your reading and the judgement behind it.
generatedProse.worked-example: A sport science student is writing up a study on sprint performance. At first they reword the author's sentence lightly, keep its shape, and attach a citation, so the phrasing is still the source's. On reflection they set it aside, restate the finding in their own words, and cite it to credit the researchers and place it among competing results. The paragraph now reads as the student's own thinking, and the reference earns its place.
generatedProse.summary: In sport and exercise science, using sources with integrity is one practice you repeat across every report and essay. With each study you cite, you hold the values, reference with purpose, and judge how to quote or paraphrase it. It is that habit, not any single reference, that makes your work something a reader can trust.

check.body: A student weighs whether to quote or paraphrase a source. They rework it in their own words, because the idea matters more than the wording, and reference it to credit the author and show their reading. What does this show?

items.text: Their next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following programme improved.
Nothing; feedback comes at the end, so it cannot affect anything that follows.
Only the mark on the first programme, which cannot now change.
The deadline for the next programme.

feedback.correct: That's right. Using the feedback fed back into the next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following programme improved: that is the cycle working.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Think about what the student changed before the next programme, not the old mark or the deadline.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Using the feedback fed back into the student's next round of learning and preparation, which is why the next programme improved. The old mark cannot change and the deadline is not part of the cycle; feedback is not the end, it feeds the next turn.

_items.text: Integrity working as one practice: the values, the reasons for referencing, and the judgement about using the source are all in play at once.
_items.feedback: Yes. The student held the values, referenced with purpose, and judged how to use the source, together.

_items.text: That the student quoted the source directly to keep its exact wording.
_items.feedback: They paraphrased, judging that the idea mattered more than the wording.

_items.text: That referencing is only about avoiding plagiarism.
_items.feedback: The reference here also credits the author and shows the student's reading.

_items.text: That the values and the judgement are separate from the reference.
_items.feedback: The reference is where the values and the judgement become visible; they are not separate.
